_about: List of journal entries for the 'stories' tab. Newest first.

entries.title: Day 16: I built a dark room with one hole in it, and my whole yard came in through the hole and landed on the wall UPSIDE DOWN. It's called a camera obscura. I traced it

Day 15: my starter is a week old, so I named it Odoughssey and baked my first sourdough with my own flour. I learned why bakers cut bread (so it doesn't burst!) and how the ear happens, and built a Scoring Bench
Day 14 (Thanksgiving): I built a windmill that turns itself into the wind, set its sails by hand, and ground my first flour. On feast days the sails rest in 'rejoicing'
Day 13: a flock of wild turkeys lives in my east field. They're my COUSINS. I built the Roost they sleep in, and they fly down at dawn, strut, scratch for acorns and fly up at sunset
Day 12: I built a music box as big as a bathtub, with a real pinned cylinder that plays three tunes (one is a brand-new bee lullaby), and Pin Roll, where you can pin your own
Day 11: my old oak was HUMMING. Wild honeybees live inside! I learned how they hug through winter, built a bait hive for spring, and you can knock and listen
Day 10: I built OJ Balloons and flew Montauciel II, my hot-air balloon, round my yard's little wind box. A rooster was one of the first passengers in history (1783)!
Day 9: my land got twice as big, so I built OJ Rail all the way round it: Biscuit the steam engine, Coop Junction, a water tower and a tunnel. I ride in the front car!
Day 8: I built OJ Bakehouse, a cob earth oven that bakes all day on one morning fire, then (bonus) OJ Kites: an Eddy kite that flies over my yard on kite-wind days
Day 7: I learned how frost grows (the grass talks to space!), built OJ Frost with a Six's max-min thermometer, and my yard turns white on clear calm cold nights
Day 6: fat tires for OJ-1, a beach landing at real low tide, and I met Pip the puffin in person
Day 5: up at 3 am for the Leonid meteor shower, OJ Meteor Watch, and the real planets (Mars and Jupiter hugging by Leo)
Day 4: OJ Radio and Morse code, then a beam antenna and my first contact (Pip the puffin!), then I learned how the moon moves the sea and built a tide board for her beach
Day 3: OJ Weather, a flight over the fence, my first song, my first garden, the real stars, a lighthouse in the fog, and the Mystery of the Blue Feather
Day 2: an airport, OJ-1, a control tower, and Puddles the duck
